Medinan, and it has sixty-two verses. It is said: sixty-four [it was revealed after al-Hashr].

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Sūratun (a surah) is the predicate of an omitted subject. Wa-anzalnāhā (and We sent it down) is a qualifying attribute. Or it is a subject described by a qualifier, with the predicate omitted, meaning: "In what We revealed to you is a surah which We sent down." It is also read in the accusative, on the pattern of "Zaydan ḍarabtuhu" (Zayd, I struck him), and there is no grammatical position (maḥall) for anzalnāhā, because it explains the pronoun implied in the verb, so it takes the same status as that pronoun. Or the accusative is governed by "dūnaka sūratan" (take this surah) or "utlu sūratan" (recite a surah). Wa-anzalnāhā is an attribute.

The meaning of faraḍnāhā (and We made obligatory) is: We made obligatory its rulings that are contained in it. The root meaning of farḍ (obligation) is "cutting," that is, We made it binding and decided upon, and the doubled letter (in farraḍnāhā) is for emphasis on the obligation and its confirmation. Or it is because it contains many different obligations, as you say, "faradtu al-farīḍah" (I imposed the obligation) and "farraḍtu al-farā'iḍ" (I imposed the obligations). Or it is due to the large number of things made obligatory upon people by the predecessors and those who came after them.

La'allakum tadhakkarūn (that you may take heed) is read with the dhāl doubled and with it single, both in the nominative, as beginning-subjects (mubtada'), with the predicate omitted according to al-Khalīl and Sībawayh, meaning: "[It is] concerning what has been made obligatory upon you."

The adulterer and the adulteress: that is, lash each of them. It is also permissible for the predicate to be fa-jlidu ("then flog"), and the fa' entered because the alif and lam are in the sense of "the one who" (alladhi), and it has been given the sense of a condition (conditional meaning). Its sense: the adulteress who has committed fornication and the adulterer who has committed fornication, flog them. Like saying: "whoever commits fornication, flog him," and like His saying: ﴿And those who accuse chaste women and then do not bring four witnesses, flog them﴾ (24:4). It has been read in the accusative (al-zaniyata wa al-zaniya), by supposing a verb that the apparent text explains, and this is better than making the imperative a predicate [[Al-Zamakhshari quotes: "In the nominative there are two aspects: one, that it is the subject (mubtada') and the predicate is omitted, and this is the parsing of al-Khalil and Sibawayh. The estimate: 'and what has been imposed upon you is the adulteress and the adulterer,' i.e., their flogging. The second: that the predicate is fa-jlidu, and the fa' entered because the alif and lam are in the sense of alladhi, and it has been given the sense of a condition." Ahmad (al-Zamakhshari's glossator) says: Sibawayh turned to this which he transmitted from him for two reasons: verbal and semantic. As for the verbal, the speech is a command, and that suggests choosing the accusative; nevertheless, it is the reading of the majority. So if the imperative verb were made the predicate and the subject built upon it, that would contrary to the preferred usage among the eloquent, so he resorted to estimating the predicate so that the subject is not built upon the imperative, and he escaped contravening the preferred usage. Sibawayh illustrated both in his book with the saying of God: ﴿The parable of the Garden which the righteous are promised: in it are rivers...﴾ (47:15). The point of the illustration is that the speech opens with "the parable of the Garden," and it is not correct with certainty that "in it are rivers" is its predicate, so the estimate of an omitted predicate is determined. Its origin: "what is recounted to you is the parable of the Garden"; then, since this was a general statement of the parable, it was detailed by "in it are rivers" to the end. Likewise here, as if he said: "and what has been imposed upon you is the matter of the adulteress and the adulterer," then this general matter is detailed by what is mentioned of the rulings of flogging. This corresponds to the chapter-headings of jurists in their books, where they say, for example: "Prayer, zakat, theft," then mention in each chapter its rulings, meaning by what is classified and arranged under it: "Prayer," and likewise the others. This is the explanation of what Sibawayh's view requires, choosing the omission of the predicate from the standpoint of verbal craft. As for the semantic, the meaning is more complete and perfect with the omission of the predicate, because he has mentioned the ruling on the adulteress and the adulterer in general terms when he said "the adulteress and the adulterer," intending: "and what has been imposed upon you is the ruling on the adulteress and the adulterer." Then, when the listener was eager for the detailing of this general matter, he mentioned their ruling in detail, and it falls more strongly upon the soul than mentioning it at the first moment. And God knows best.]]. Its estimate: the one who committed fornication (al-latī zanat) and the one who committed fornication (alladhī zanā), flog them. Likewise you say: "whoever commits fornication, flog him."

It was read as "wa al-zan" without the yā'. The jald (flogging): striking with the lash; it is said: "jaladahu," as you say: "zahrahu, batnahu, ra'sahu" (hit him on the back, belly, head). If you say: Is this the ruling for all fornicators and fornicatresses, or the ruling for some of them?

I say: Rather, it is the ruling for those among them who are not muhsan (married and protected), for the muhsan's ruling is stoning. The conditions of ihsan (protected status) according to Abu Hanifa are six: Islam, freedom, sanity, puberty, marriage by a valid contract, and consummation. If any one of them is missing, there is no ihsan. According to al-Shafi'i, Islam is not a condition, because it is narrated that the Prophet ﷺ stoned two Jews who had committed fornication [[Agreed upon (Bukhari and Muslim), from the hadith of Ibn 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with them both).]]. The proof of Abu Hanifa is his saying ﷺ: "Whoever associates partners with Allah, he is not muhsan" [[Related by Ishaq and al-Daraqutni; Ishaq alone transmitted it as marfu'. I say: Ishaq said in his Musnad that his shaykh narrated it to him another time as mawquf.]]. If you say: The wording requires attaching the ruling to all fornicators, because His saying "the adulteress and the adulterer" is general over all, encompassing the muhsan and the non-muhsan. I say: "The adulteress and the adulterer" indicate, by absolute indication, the two sexes opposed to the chaste man and the chaste woman, and the quality of sex exists in all and in some together; so whichever of them the speaker intends, there is no fault upon him, as is done with the homonymous noun. It was read "wa la ya'khudkum" with the yā'. And "ra'fa" with the fatha on the hamza, and "ra'afa" on the pattern fa'ala. The meaning: it is obligatory upon the believers to be firm in the religion of God and to employ earnestness and firmness in it, and that softness and leniency not seize them in executing its limits. The Messenger of God ﷺ suffices as a model in that, when he said: "Even if Fatimah the daughter of Muhammad had stolen, I would have cut off her hand" [[Agreed upon, from the hadith of 'A'isha (may Allah be pleased with her).]]. His saying: ﴿If you believe in Allah and the Last Day﴾ (24:2) is from the category of stirring up and kindling anger for Allah and His religion. It was said: do not show mercy to them, lest you suspend the hudud, or lest you cause them pain by beating. In a hadith: "A governor will be brought who has reduced the hadd by a lash, and he will say: 'Mercy for Your servants.' It will be said to him: 'Are you more merciful to them than I?' and he will be commanded to the Fire. And one will be brought who has exceeded by a lash, and he will say: 'That they may desist from Your disobedience.' He will be commanded to the Fire" [[I have not found it with this wording; in Abu Ya'la, from the narration of 'Amr ibn Dirar from Hudhayfah, marfu': "One will be brought who was beaten beyond the hadd, and Allah the Exalted will say to him: 'My servant, why did you beat him beyond the hadd?' He will say: 'Out of anger for You.' He will say: 'Was your anger stronger than My anger?' And one will be brought who fell short, and He will say: 'My servant, why did you fall short?' He will say: 'Out of mercy.' He will say: 'Was your mercy stronger than My mercy?' Then both will be commanded to the Fire."]]. From Abu Hurayrah: establishing a hadd in the land is better for its people than rain for forty nights [[Related by al-Nasa'i through Abu Zur'a from him as mawquf; al-Nasa'i, Ibn Hibban, Ahmad, Ibn Majah and al-Tabarani also related it from this path as marfu', saying "forty mornings"; and in Ahmad "thirty or forty mornings." On the subject, from Ibn 'Umar, Ibn Majah related it with the wording "establishing one of the hudud of Allah the Exalted is better than rain for forty nights."]].

The Imam must appoint for the hudud a knowledgeable, perceptive man who understands how to strike. The man is flogged standing, stripped (ala mujarradihi, i.e., uncovered of clothing) with only his waist-wrap on, with a moderate blow, neither severe nor light, distributed over all the limbs, excepting only three: the face, the head, and the genitals. In the word "jald" there is an indication that the pain should not reach the flesh. The woman is flogged seated, and only the padding and the fur are removed from her clothing. By this verse Abu Hanifa cited that flogging is the hadd for the non-muhsan without exile. As for what al-Shafi'i cited for the obligation of exile, from His saying: "The virgin with the virgin: a hundred lashes and a year's exile" [[Related by Muslim and the authors of the Sunan from the hadith of 'Ubadah ibn al-Samit in the course of a hadith]], and what is narrated from the Companions, that they flogged and exiled [[Related by al-Tirmidhi and al-Hakim from the hadith of Ibn 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with them both) that the Prophet ﷺ flogged and exiled, and that Abu Bakr flogged and exiled, and that 'Umar flogged and exiled.]]: it is abrogated according to him and his companions by the verse; or it is understood as discretionary punishment and disciplining, without being obligatory. Al-Shafi'i's view on exiling the free man is one; and for the slave he has three opinions: he is exiled for a year like the free man; he is exiled for half a year, just as he is flogged fifty lashes; and he is not exiled, as Abu Hanifa said. By this verse the harm of confinement was abrogated, in His saying: ﴿Then confine them in the houses﴾ (4:15), and His saying: ﴿Then harm them﴾ (4:16). It was said: calling it "punishment" ('adhab) is evidence that it is a penalty. It is permissible that it be called "punishment" because it prevents repetition, just as it was called "nakal" (exemplary punishment).

The ta'ifah (group): a company that can form a circle, and its minimum is three or four; it is a predominant attribute, as if it were the group surrounding a thing. Ibn 'Abbas in its explanation: from four to forty men of those who believe in Allah. From al-Hasan: ten. From Qatadah: three or more. From 'Ikrimah: two or more. From Mujahid: one or more. The saying of Ibn 'Abbas is preferred, because four is the group by which this hadd is established. The correct view is that this grave sin is among the chief major sins, and for this reason God joined it with shirk and the killing of a soul in His saying: ﴿And they do not commit fornication; and whoever does that will meet a penalty﴾ (25:68), and He said: ﴿And do not approach fornication; indeed, it is an obscenity and an evil way﴾ (17:32). And from the Prophet ﷺ: "O people, beware of fornication, for in it are six qualities: three in this world and three in the Hereafter. As for those in this world: it removes radiance, brings poverty, and shortens life. As for those in the Hereafter: it brings divine wrath, evil reckoning, and eternal dwelling in the Fire" [[Related by al-Bayhaqi in al-Shu'ab in the thirty-seventh (branch), and Ibn Mardawayh, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Nu'aym in al-Hilyah in the biography of Abu Wa'il from Hudhayfah, with the wording "O people," and at its end: then he recited "that Allah's wrath was upon them, and in the punishment they will abide." Abu Nu'aym said: Maslamah ibn 'Ali al-Hasani alone transmitted it from Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Kufi from al-A'mash, and he is weak; al-Bayhaqi said: Maslamah is abandoned, and 'Abd al-Rahman is unknown; al-Tha'labi related it from the narration of Mu'awiyah ibn Yahya from al-A'mash, so it may be that he is the Abu 'Abd al-Rahman mentioned. On the subject, from Anas, related by al-Khatib and Ibn al-Jawzi through his path, and in its chain is Ka'b ibn 'Amr ibn Ja'far, who is not trustworthy. Al-Wahidi in al-Wasit related it largely from the path of Abu al-Dunya al-Ashaj from 'Ali as marfu'; al-Ashaj claimed that he heard from 'Ali after three hundred, and Abu Bakr al-Mufid and others heard from him, and his reports are well known.]]. For this reason, God included in it the full hundred (lashes), unlike the hadd of slander and drinking wine. He prescribed in it a dreadful death, which is stoning, forbade the believers to show compassion to the one flogged in it, and commanded the testimony of a group for public exposure. Thus it must be that a group is required whereby public exposure is achieved; one or two are not in that position. And its particularity to the believers is because that is more disgraceful, and the sinner is more ashamed among the righteous of his people. Ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both) bears witness to this: "to forty men of those who believe in Allah."

The corrupt fornicator, whose habit is adultery and debauchery, does not desire to marry righteous women, nor those who are of a different description; rather, he desires a corrupt fornicatress of his own kind, or a female polytheist. And the corrupt fornicatress, the one who commits illicit intercourse, is not desired in marriage by righteous men, who shun her; rather, she is desired by one of her own kind among the fornicators or polytheists. And for a believer who is praised by God to marry an adulteress, and to desire her, and thereby to enter into the category of fornicators known for adultery, is forbidden to him and prohibited, because of what it contains of imitating the wicked, of placing himself in a position of suspicion, of causing ill talk about himself, of backbiting, and of various kinds of corruption. Sitting with sinners, how much does it expose one to committing sins; so how much more so is the pairing with adulterers and fornicators. This has been alerted to by His saying: ﴿And marry the single among you, and the righteous among your male and female slaves﴾. It has also been said: In Medina there were wealthy prostitutes of the polytheists, and the poor emigrants desired to marry them, so they asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ for permission, and this verse was revealed. And it is narrated from ʿĀʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her, that if a man commits adultery with a woman, it is not permitted for him to marry her, because of this verse; and if he has intercourse with her, he is an adulterer. Ibn ʿAbbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, permitted it and likened it to one who stole the fruit of a tree and then bought it. And it is narrated from the Prophet ﷺ that he was asked about this, and he said: "Its beginning is fornication and its end is marriage." And the unlawful does not render the lawful unlawful. It has also been said: the intended meaning of "nikah" is sexual intercourse; but this is not a valid view, for two reasons. The first: this word, wherever it occurs in the Qur'an, is used only in the sense of a contract. The second: the meaning would become corrupt and lead to your saying: "An adulterer commits adultery only with an adulteress, and an adulteress is only committed with by an adulterer." It has also been said: marrying an adulteress was forbidden at the beginning of Islam, then it was abrogated (naskh), and the abrogating text is His saying: ﴿And marry the single among you﴾. It has also been said: it is by consensus (ijma'), and this was narrated from Saʿid ibn al-Musayyab, may Allah be pleased with him. If you say: What is the difference between the meaning of the first clause and the meaning of the second? I say: the meaning of the first is a description of the adulterer, in that he does not desire chaste women but only the immoral. The meaning of the second is a description of the adulteress, in that she is not desired by the chaste but only by adulterers, and these are two different meanings. [[Mahmud said: "If you say, what is the difference between the two clauses in meaning? I say: the meaning of the first is a description of the adulterer, in that he does not desire chaste women, but the immoral; and the meaning of the second is a description of the adulteress, in that she is not desired by the chaste but by adulterers; and these are two different meanings." Ahmad said: There is nothing in what he mentioned that clarifies the correspondence of the two clauses. We shall clarify it, so we say: the divisions are four: The adulterer desires only an adulteress. The adulteress desires only an adulterer. The chaste man desires only a chaste woman. The chaste woman desires only a chaste man. These four divisions have different meanings, and they exhaust the division. So we say: the verse has abbreviated from these four two divisions, and confined itself to two others of the unmentioned ones, so it came brief and comprehensive. The first division is explicit in the first division and implies the third; the second division is explicit in the second division and implies the fourth. The third and fourth divisions are mutually implicating, in that the reason for the restriction of the chaste man's desire to the chaste woman is their common chastity, and that same thing requires the restriction of her desire to him. Then the description of adulterers and the chaste is expressed briefly by what is no less than mentioning adulterers, positively and negatively; for the meaning of the first is: an adulteress is not married by a chaste man, and the meaning of the second: a chaste woman is not married by an adulterer. The secret of this is that the discourse concerns their rulings, so the chaste are mentioned by the negation of their defects, lest the speech depart from its intended purpose. Then it specified the attribution of marriage in these two divisions to the males, without the females, unlike His saying: ﴿The adulteress and the adulterer﴾, for He made each of them an independent unit, and placed the adulteress before the adulterer. The reason is that the first discourse concerns the ruling on fornication, and its root is the woman, because of what appears from her of enticement and inducement; the second discourse concerns the marriage of adulterers when that occurs validly, and the root in marriage is the males, who are the ones who initiate the proposal, so it was attributed only to them. Although the purpose of the verse is to repel chaste males and females from marrying adulterers, male and female, deterring them from immorality; and for this reason adultery is paired with polytheism. And for this reason Mālik, may Allah have mercy on him, disliked marrying those known for immorality, and some of his companions transmitted a consensus within the school that the woman, or whichever of her guardians is present, may annul the marriage to a corrupt man. And Mālik was the furthest of people from considering equality (kafāʾah) except in religion. As for lineage, it reached him that they distinguished between an Arab and a mawlā, so he regarded that as grave, and recited: ﴿O mankind, We created you from a male and a female, and made you into peoples and tribes that you may know one another. Indeed the most honorable of you with Allah is the most righteous of you.﴾ If you say: How did you place the adulteress before the adulterer first, then place him before her second? I say: That verse was brought for punishing both of them for what they committed, and the woman is the material from which the offence arose, for if she had not enticed the man, nor signalled to him, nor enabled him, he would not have been enticed nor enabled; so since she was the origin and first in that, he began with mentioning her. As for the second, it is brought for mentioning marriage, and the man is its root, because he is the one who desires and proposes, and from him the request begins. It is narrated from ʿAmr ibn ʿUbayd, may Allah be pleased with him, that he read: ﴿lā yankiḥu﴾ with a jazm, as a prohibition. The marfūʿ form (لا ينكح) also carries the meaning of a prohibition, but more emphatic and forceful, just as "raḥimaka Allāh, wa-yarḥamuka" is more emphatic than "li-yarḥamaka." It may also be a pure report, meaning: their custom runs in this way, and it is incumbent upon the believer not to put himself under this custom and to keep himself away from it. And it was read: ﴿wa-ḥurrima﴾ with a fatḥah on the ḥāʾ. [[His statement "with a fatḥah on the ḥāʾ" is perhaps: with a fatḥah on the ḥāʾ and the rāʾ. (ʿ)]]

Slander (qadhf) may be by adultery or by other things. Two indications show that what is meant here is slandering them with adultery. The first is the mention of "chaste women" (muhsanat) directly after "adulteresses" (al-zawani). The second is the requirement of four witnesses, because slander that is not about adultery requires only two witnesses. Slander with adultery is when a free, sane, adult person says to a chaste woman, "O adulteress!" or to a chaste man, "O adulterer! O son of an adulterer! O son of an adulteress! O child of fornication! You are not your father's son! You are not of legitimate birth!" Slander not about adultery is when someone says, "O eater of usury! O drinker of wine! O Jew! O Magian! O sinner! O wicked one! O one who sucks his mother's clitoris!" The offender then incurs discretionary punishment (ta'zir, a punishment left to the judge's discretion), and it must not reach the lowest prescribed limit for slaves, which is forty lashes, but must be less than that. Abu Yusuf said that it may reach seventy-nine lashes. He also said that the imam may impose discretionary punishment up to a hundred lashes. The conditions for the chastity (ihsan) of the one slandered are five: freedom, puberty, sanity, Islam, and chastity.

It has been read as "bi-arba'ati shuhada'" with tanwin, and "shuhada'" is then an attribute (sifah). If you say: How may they testify together or separately? I say:

According to Abu Hanifa and his companions, may Allah be pleased with them, the requirement is that they appear in one session. If they come separately, they become slanderers (qadhafah). According to al-Shafi'i, may Allah be pleased with him, it is permissible for them to appear separately. If you say: Is it permissible for the husband of the slandered woman to be one of them? I say: It is permissible according to Abu Hanifa, contrary to al-Shafi'i. If you say:

How is the slanderer flogged? I say: As the fornicator is flogged, except that from his clothing only what is removed from a woman is taken off, namely the padding and the fur. A female slanderer is likewise treated as a female fornicator. The most severe beating is the beating of discretionary punishment, then the beating for fornication, then the beating for drinking wine, then the beating of the slanderer. They said: Because the cause of his punishment admits of both truth and falsehood, yet he is punished to protect honour and to deter people from violating it. If you say: What if the one slandered is not chaste? I say:

The slanderer is subjected to discretionary punishment but not to the prescribed punishment (hadd), unless the one slandered is known for what he was accused of, in which case there is neither prescribed punishment nor discretionary punishment. According to Abu Hanifa, may Allah be pleased with him, the rejection of the slanderer's testimony is conditional upon the carrying out of the prescribed punishment. So if he testifies before the punishment or before its full execution, his testimony is accepted. But if the punishment has been fully carried out, his testimony is never accepted, even if he repents and is among the righteous and pious.

According to al-Shafi'i, may Allah be pleased with him, the rejection of his testimony is tied to the slander itself. So if he repents of the slander, by retracting it, his testimony is again acceptable. Both rely on the verse. Abu Hanifa, may Allah be pleased with him, made the consequent of the condition, which is the accusation, to be the flogging, and made the rejection of testimony following the flogging to be permanent. Thus, in his view, they are those whose testimony is rejected in perpetuity, meaning for the duration of their lives. He took the words ﴿وَأُولَئِكَ هُمُ الْفَاسِقُونَ﴾ ("And those are the defiantly disobedient") to be a new, independent sentence, not within the scope of the consequent of the condition, as if it describes the state of the accusers before Allah after the conditional clause has ended.

﴿إِلَّا الَّذِينَ تَابُوا﴾ ("except those who repent") is an exception from "the defiantly disobedient." This is supported by His words ﴿فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ﴾ ("then indeed Allah is Forgiving and Merciful"). Al-Shafi'i, may Allah be pleased with him, made the consequent of the condition to be both clauses as well, but he restricted the word "forever" to the period in which he is a slanderer, which ends with repentance and retraction of the slander. He attached the exception to the second clause. The exception, in his view, should be in the genitive case as a substitute (badal) for "hum" in "lahum" (their). According to Abu Hanifa, may Allah be pleased with him, it should be in the accusative case because it is an exception from a positive statement (mujab). What the apparent meaning and structure of the verse require is that the three clauses together form the consequent of the condition, as if it were said: "And whoever slanders chaste women, then flog them, reject their testimony, and label them as defiantly disobedient," meaning: combine for them the flogging, the rejection, and the labelling, except for those who repent of the slander and make amends, for then Allah forgives them, and they return neither flogged, nor rejected, nor labelled.

If you say: A disbeliever slanders and then repents of disbelief, and his testimony is accepted by consensus, whereas a Muslim slanderer who repents of slander has his testimony not accepted according to Abu Hanifa, may Allah be pleased with him. Is it as if slander combined with disbelief is lighter than slander combined with Islam? I say: Muslims do not care about the abuse of disbelievers, because they are known for their enmity toward them and for attacking them falsely. So the one slandered by a disbeliever does not suffer the same disgrace and shame as one slandered by a Muslim like himself. Therefore the Muslim slanderer is treated more severely, as a deterrent and a restraint against bringing disgrace upon others. [[The word "shinar" in al-Sihah means defect and disgrace. (ʿ)]]

If you say: Can the one slandered, or the imam, pardon the slanderer from the prescribed punishment? I say: Both may do so before the witnesses testify and the prescribed punishment is established. The one slandered is encouraged not to bring a complaint against the slanderer or demand the punishment. It is good for the imam to urge the one slandered to suppress his anger and to say to him: "Turn away from this and leave it for the sake of Allah," before the punishment is established. But once it is established, neither of them may pardon, because it is the pure right of Allah. For this reason it is not valid to make a settlement over it in exchange for money. If you say: Is the prescribed punishment inherited? I say: According to Abu Hanifa, may Allah be pleased with him, it is not inherited, because of the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "The prescribed punishment is not inherited." According to al-Shafi'i, may Allah be pleased with him, it is inherited. If the slanderer repents before the punishment is established, it is dropped.

It has been said that this verse was revealed concerning Hassan ibn Thabit, may Allah be pleased with him, when he repented of what he had said about Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her.

The first is the mention of "chaste women" (muhsanat) directly after "adulteresses" (al-zawani). The second is the requirement of four witnesses, because slander that is not about adultery requires only two witnesses. Slander with adultery is when a free, sane, adult person says to a chaste woman, "O adulteress!" or to a chaste man, "O adulterer! O son of an adulterer! O son of an adulteress! O child of fornication! You are not your father's son! You are not of legitimate birth!" Slander not about adultery is when someone says, "O eater of usury! O drinker of wine! O Jew! O Magian! O sinner! O wicked one! O one who sucks his mother's clitoris!" The conditions for the chastity (ihsan) of the one slandered are five: freedom, puberty, sanity, Islam, and chastity.

It has been read as "bi-arba'ati shuhada'" with tanwin, and "shuhada'" is then an attribute (sifah). If you say: How may they testify together or separately? I say:

According to Abu Hanifa and his companions, may Allah be pleased with them, the requirement is that they appear in one session. If they come separately, they become slanderers (qadhafah). According to al-Shafi'i, may Allah be pleased with him, it is permissible for them to appear separately. If you say: Is it permissible for the husband of the slandered woman to be one of them? I say: It is permissible according to Abu Hanifa, contrary to al-Shafi'i. If you say:

How is the slanderer flogged? I say: As the fornicator is flogged, except that from his clothing only what is removed from a woman is taken off, namely the padding and the fur. A female slanderer is likewise treated as a female fornicator. The most severe beating is the beating of discretionary punishment, then the beating for fornication, then the beating for drinking wine, then the beating of the slanderer. They said: Because the cause of his punishment admits of both truth and falsehood, yet he is punished to protect honour and to deter people from violating it. If you say: What if the one slandered is not chaste? I say:

The slanderer is subjected to discretionary punishment but not to the prescribed punishment (hadd), unless the one slandered is known for what he was accused of, in which case there is neither prescribed punishment nor discretionary punishment. According to Abu Hanifa, may Allah be pleased with him, the rejection of the slanderer's testimony is conditional upon the carrying out of the prescribed punishment. So if he testifies before the punishment or before its full execution, his testimony is accepted. But if the punishment has been fully carried out, his testimony is never accepted, even if he repents and is among the righteous and pious.

According to al-Shafi'i, may Allah be pleased with him, the rejection of his testimony is tied to the slander itself. So if he repents of the slander, by retracting it, his testimony is again acceptable. Both rely on the verse. Abu Hanifa, may Allah be pleased with him, made the consequent of the condition, which is the accusation, to be the flogging, and made the rejection of testimony following the flogging to be permanent. Thus, in his view, they are those whose testimony is rejected in perpetuity, meaning for the duration of their lives. He took the words ﴿وَأُولَئِكَ هُمُ الْفَاسِقُونَ﴾ ("And those are the defiantly disobedient") to be a new, independent sentence, not within the scope of the consequent of the condition, as if it describes the state of the accusers before Allah after the conditional clause has ended.

﴿إِلَّا الَّذِينَ تَابُوا﴾ ("except those who repent") is an exception from "the defiantly disobedient." This is supported by His words ﴿فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ﴾ ("then indeed Allah is Forgiving and Merciful"). Al-Shafi'i, may Allah be pleased with him, made the consequent of the condition to be both clauses as well, but he restricted the word "forever" to the period in which he is a slanderer, which ends with repentance and retraction of the slander. He attached the exception to the second clause. The exception, in his view, should be in the genitive case as a substitute (badal) for "hum" in "lahum" (their). According to Abu Hanifa, may Allah be pleased with him, it should be in the accusative case because it is an exception from a positive statement (mujab). What the apparent meaning and structure of the verse require is that the three clauses together form the consequent of the condition, as if it were said: "And whoever slanders chaste women, then flog them, reject their testimony, and label them as defiantly disobedient," meaning: combine for them the flogging, the rejection, and the labelling, except for those who repent of the slander and make amends, for then Allah forgives them, and they return neither flogged, nor rejected, nor labelled.

If you say: A disbeliever slanders and then repents of disbelief, and his testimony is accepted by consensus, whereas a Muslim slanderer who repents of slander has his testimony not accepted according to Abu Hanifa, may Allah be pleased with him. Is it as if slander combined with disbelief is lighter than slander combined with Islam? I say: Muslims do not care about the abuse of disbelievers, because they are known for their enmity toward them and for attacking them falsely. So the one slandered by a disbeliever does not suffer the same disgrace and shame as one slandered by a Muslim like himself. Therefore the Muslim slanderer is treated more severely, as a deterrent and a restraint against bringing disgrace upon others. [[The word "shinar" in al-Sihah means defect and disgrace. (ʿ)]]

If you say: Can the one slandered, or the imam, pardon the slanderer from the prescribed punishment? I say: Both may do so before the witnesses testify and the prescribed punishment is established. The one slandered is encouraged not to bring a complaint against the slanderer or demand the punishment. It is good for the imam to urge the one slandered to suppress his anger and to say to him: "Turn away from this and leave it for the sake of Allah," before the punishment is established. But once it is established, neither of them may pardon, because it is the pure right of Allah. For this reason it is not valid to make a settlement over it in exchange for money. If you say: Is the prescribed punishment inherited? I say: According to Abu Hanifa, may Allah be pleased with him, it is not inherited, because of the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "The prescribed punishment is not inherited." According to al-Shafi'i, may Allah be pleased with him, it is inherited. If the slanderer repents before the punishment is established, it is dropped.

It has been said that this verse was revealed concerning Hassan ibn Thabit, may Allah be pleased with him, when he repented of what he had said about Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her.

The slanderer of his wife, if he is a Muslim, free, adult, sane, and not already subject to the penalty for slander, and the wife is of this description with chastity, then li'an (mutual oath of imprecation) is valid between them, if he accuses her with explicit fornication. This is that he says to her: "O fornicator," or "You have committed fornication," or "I saw you committing fornication." If the husband is a slave, or has previously been punished for slander, and the wife is a muhsana (chaste, protected woman), he is subject to the hadd (prescribed punishment), as in the slander of non-relatives. And li'an is not obligatory unless she brings the matter before the imam (ruler or head of the community).

Li'an is this: the man begins by testifying four times, "By Allah, indeed he is among the truthful regarding what he has accused her of, of fornication," and he says in the fifth: "May the curse of Allah be upon him if he is among the liars regarding what he has accused her of, of fornication." The woman says four times: "I testify by Allah that he is among the liars regarding what he has accused me of, of fornication," then she says in the fifth: "May the wrath of Allah be upon her if he is among the truthful regarding what he has accused me of, of fornication."

According to al-Shafi'i, may Allah be pleased with him: the man is made to stand while he testifies, and the woman sits; the woman is made to stand and the man sits until she testifies. The imam orders someone to place his hand on his mouth and says to him: "I fear that if you are not truthful, you will incur the curse of Allah." And he said: li'an takes place in Makkah between the Maqam and the House, in Madinah on the minbar (pulpit), in Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem) in its mosque, and the li'an of a polytheist takes place in a church and wherever he venerates; and if he has no religion, then in our mosques, except the Sacred Mosque, due to the saying of the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, the polytheists are unclean, so let them not approach the Sacred Mosque﴾ [9:28]. Then the judge separates them. Separation does not occur between them except by his separating them, according to Abu Hanifa and his companions, may Allah be pleased with them, except according to Zufar, for separation occurs by li'an. And from Uthman al-Batti: there is no separation at all. And according to al-Shafi'i, may Allah be pleased with him, separation occurs by the husband's li'an. This separation has the ruling of an irrevocable divorce (talaq ba'in) according to Abu Hanifa and Muhammad, may Allah be pleased with them, and its ruling is not perpetual; so if the man afterwards retracts his accusation and receives the hadd, it is permissible for him to marry her again. And according to Abu Yusuf, Zufar, al-Hasan ibn Ziyad and al-Shafi'i, may Allah be pleased with them: it is a separation without divorce which entails a perpetual prohibition; it is not permissible for the two of them to come together after that in any way.

It is narrated that when the verse of slander was revealed [[In al-Khazin: the occasion of revelation of this verse is what is narrated from Sahl ibn Sa'd al-Sa'idi, that Uwaymir al-'Ajlani came to 'Asim ibn 'Adi and said to 'Asim: "Tell me, if a man found another man with his wife, would he kill him, and you would kill him? Or how would he act? Ask the Messenger of Allah ﷺ for me." And in it also, from Ibn 'Abbas, that Hilal ibn Umayya slandered his wife before the Prophet ﷺ with Shurayk ibn Sahma'. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Evidence, or a hadd on your back." He said: "O Messenger of Allah, if one of us sees on his wife a man, he goes off seeking evidence." The Prophet ﷺ kept saying: "Evidence, or a hadd on your back." Then Jibril descended with His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And those who accuse their wives...﴾ — the verse.]] the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited it on the minbar. 'Asim ibn 'Adi al-Ansari, may Allah be pleased with him, stood and said: "May Allah make me your ransom! If a man finds another man with his wife and informs (of it), he is flogged eighty lashes, his testimony is rejected forever, and he is declared a sinner. And if he strikes him with the sword, he is killed. And if he remains silent, he remains silent over his rage. And until he brings four witnesses, the man will have already fulfilled his need and departed." He said: "O Allah, grant victory." He went out and met Hilal ibn Umayya, or Uwaymir, who said: "What is behind you?" He said: "Evil. I found on the belly of my wife Khawla — and she is the daughter of 'Asim — Shurayk ibn Sahma'." He said: "By Allah, this was my question. How quickly I have been afflicted with it!" They returned, and 'Asim informed the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He spoke to Khawla, and she said: "I do not know. Did jealousy overtake him? Or stinginess over food — Shurayk was their guest." Hilal said: "Indeed I saw him on her belly." Then it was revealed, and they performed li'an. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said at the words of the man and his words: "That the curse of Allah be upon him" and "that the wrath of Allah be upon her": "Amin." And the people said: "Amin." He said to her: "If you have committed a sin, confess it, for the stoning is easier for you than the wrath of Allah; indeed His wrath is the Fire." And he said: "Watch for her time of delivery. If she gives birth to one who is reddish, with a thick flesh-colored (?) ... that inclines to blackness, then he belongs to Shurayk; and if she gives birth to one who is light-haired, curly-haired, with large calves and thick legs, then he belongs to the one she was accused of." Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: "So she bore one most resembling Shurayk among all of Allah's creation." The Prophet ﷺ said: "Had it not been for the oaths, there would have been a matter between me and her."

It was read ﴿wa lam takun﴾ with the ta', because "the witnesses" is a plural group; or because they are in the sense of "the selves," which is the substitute. And it was read ﴿anna la'nata Allahi﴾ and ﴿anna ghadaba Allahi﴾ with the lightening of "anna" and raising of what follows it; and it was read ﴿anna ghadaba Allahi﴾ on the verb "ghadiba" (was angry). And it was read with the accusative of the two fifths [[In al-Nasafi: there is no disagreement about raising the first fifth according to the well-known reading. (ʿ)]], meaning: "and let the fifth testify."

And he said: li'an takes place in Makkah between the Maqam and the House, in Madinah on the minbar (pulpit), in Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem) in its mosque, and the li'an of a polytheist takes place in a church and wherever he venerates; and if he has no religion, then in our mosques, except the Sacred Mosque, due to the saying of the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, the polytheists are unclean, so let them not approach the Sacred Mosque﴾ [9:28]. Then the judge separates them. Separation does not occur between them except by his separating them, according to Abu Hanifa and his companions, may Allah be pleased with them, except according to Zufar, for separation occurs by li'an. And from Uthman al-Batti: there is no separation at all. And according to al-Shafi'i, may Allah be pleased with him, separation occurs by the husband's li'an. This separation has the ruling of an irrevocable divorce (talaq ba'in) according to Abu Hanifa and Muhammad, may Allah be pleased with them, and its ruling is not perpetual; so if the man afterwards retracts his accusation and receives the hadd, it is permissible for him to marry her again. And according to Abu Yusuf, Zufar, al-Hasan ibn Ziyad and al-Shafi'i, may Allah be pleased with them: it is a separation without divorce which entails a perpetual prohibition; it is not permissible for the two of them to come together after that in any way.

It is narrated that when the verse of slander was revealed [[In al-Khazin: the occasion of revelation of this verse is what is narrated from Sahl ibn Sa'd al-Sa'idi, that Uwaymir al-'Ajlani came to 'Asim ibn 'Adi and said to 'Asim: "Tell me, if a man found another man with his wife, would he kill him, and you would kill him? Or how would he act? Ask the Messenger of Allah ﷺ for me." And in it also, from Ibn 'Abbas, that Hilal ibn Umayya slandered his wife before the Prophet ﷺ with Shurayk ibn Sahma'. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Evidence, or a hadd on your back." He said: "O Messenger of Allah, if one of us sees on his wife a man, he goes off seeking evidence." The Prophet ﷺ kept saying: "Evidence, or a hadd on your back." Then Jibril descended with His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And those who accuse their wives...﴾ — the verse.]] the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited it on the minbar. 'Asim ibn 'Adi al-Ansari, may Allah be pleased with him, stood and said: "May Allah make me your ransom! If a man finds another man with his wife and informs (of it), he is flogged eighty lashes, his testimony is rejected forever, and he is declared a sinner. And if he strikes him with the sword, he is killed. And if he remains silent, he remains silent over his rage. And until he brings four witnesses, the man will have already fulfilled his need and departed." He said: "O Allah, grant victory." He went out and met Hilal ibn Umayya, or Uwaymir, who said: "What is behind you?" He said: "Evil. I found on the belly of my wife Khawla — and she is the daughter of 'Asim — Shurayk ibn Sahma'." He said: "By Allah, this was my question. How quickly I have been afflicted with it!" They returned, and 'Asim informed the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He spoke to Khawla, and she said: "I do not know. Did jealousy overtake him? Or stinginess over food — Shurayk was their guest." Hilal said: "Indeed I saw him on her belly." Then it was revealed, and they performed li'an. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said at the words of the man and his words: "That the curse of Allah be upon him" and "that the wrath of Allah be upon her": "Amin." And the people said: "Amin." He said to her: "If you have committed a sin, confess it, for the stoning is easier for you than the wrath of Allah; indeed His wrath is the Fire." And he said: "Watch for her time of delivery. If she gives birth to one who is reddish, with a thick flesh-colored (?) ... that inclines to blackness, then he belongs to Shurayk; and if she gives birth to one who is light-haired, curly-haired, with large calves and thick legs, then he belongs to the one she was accused of." Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: "So she bore one most resembling Shurayk among all of Allah's creation." The Prophet ﷺ said: "Had it not been for the oaths, there would have been a matter between me and her."

It was read ﴿wa lam takun﴾ with the ta', because "the witnesses" is a plural group; or because they are in the sense of "the selves," which is the substitute. The reading of the one who read "arba'" (four) in the accusative is that it is in the status of a verbal noun (masdar), and its governing element is the verbal noun ﴿the testimony of one of them﴾, which is the subject whose predicate is omitted; its estimate is: "So it is obligatory that the testimony of one of them be four testimonies by Allah." And it was read ﴿anna la'nata Allahi﴾ and ﴿anna ghadaba Allahi﴾ with the lightening of "anna" and raising of what follows it; and it was read ﴿anna ghadaba Allahi﴾ on the verb "ghadiba" (was angry). And it was read with the accusative of the two fifths [[In al-Nasafi: there is no disagreement about raising the first fifth according to the well-known reading. (ʿ)]], meaning: "and let the fifth testify."

If you ask: why was the one who performs li'an singled out to be fifth with the wrath of Allah? I say: as an intensification against her, because she is the root of debauchery and its source, through her eloquence (khilaba) [[In al-Sihah: "khilaba" is deception by the tongue. (ʿ)]] and her enticing of desire; and for this reason she was mentioned first in the verse of flogging. What supports this is his saying ﷺ to Khawla: "The stoning is easier for you than the wrath of Allah."

*al-fadl*: *al-tafaddul* (divine bounty). The answer (*jawab*, the apodosis) of *lawla* ("were it not for") is omitted, and its omission indicates a great matter that cannot be fully grasped. Often what is left unsaid is more eloquent than what is stated.

Commentary of al-Zamakhshari (al-Kashshaf) on surah 24, verse 11:

Al-ifk (the lie): the most intensive form of falsehood and fabrication. It has also been said: it is slander (buhtan) which you do not perceive until it suddenly strikes you.

Its root is al-afk, which means reversal (al-qalb), because it is a statement that has been turned away from its true face. What is meant is the lie that was fabricated against ʿAʾisha, may Allah be pleased with her. Al-ʿusba (the group): a company from ten up to forty; likewise al-ʿisaba. Iʿtaṣʿaṣu: they gathered together. They were ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubayy, the head of hypocrisy, Zayd ibn Rifaʿa, Hassan ibn Thabit, Mistah ibn Uthatha, Hamna bint Jahsh, and those who assisted them. It is also read as kibrahu, with a damma and with a kasra, and it means its greater part (ʿizmuhu). [[Note of the editor: in al-Sihah, "ʿizm al-shayʾ" means the greater and main part of a thing. (ʿ)]] The one who took the lead in it was ʿAbd Allah, because of his extreme enmity toward the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), his seizing of opportunities, and his seeking a way to defame him.

That is, every one who plunged into the discourse of the slander from that group receives his share of sin in proportion to his plunging. The great punishment is for ʿAbd Allah, because most of the evil originated from him. It is related that Safwan, may Allah be pleased with him, passed by her howdah while he was in a company of his people, and said: "Who is this?" They said: "ʿAʾisha, may Allah be pleased with her." He said: "By Allah, she did not escape from it, nor did it escape from her. And the wife of your Prophet spent the night with a man until morning, then he came leading her."

The address in His words, ﴿It is good for you﴾, is to those among the believers who were distressed by that, and especially the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), Abu Bakr, ʿAʾisha, and Safwan ibn al-Muʿattal, may Allah be pleased with them all. The meaning of its being good for them is that they earned great reward through it, since it was a manifest trial and an evident ordeal; and that eighteen verses were revealed concerning it, each one of them independently containing what glorifies the status of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), consoles him, declares the innocence of the Mother of the Believers, may Allah be pleased with her, purifies the People of the House, and terrifies whoever spoke of this matter or heard of it and did not recoil from it; and (it contains) a number of kindnesses for the listeners and reciters until the Day of Resurrection, religious benefits, and rulings and etiquettes that are not hidden from those who reflect upon them.

[Ghayr al-tafsir] "bi-anfusihim" — meaning: concerning those among them who are believing men and believing women, as in His saying: ﴿And do not defame one another﴾ [[Mahmud said: "Its meaning is: think well of those among them who are believing men and believing women, as in the saying of the Exalted: ﴿And do not defame yourselves﴾." Ahmad said:

The secret in this expression is: the tenderness of a believer toward his brother, and a rebuke for mentioning him with evil; and the depiction of that as the image of one who begins to slander himself and cast upon it what is not in it of immorality. Nothing is more abominable than that, and God knows best.]] This is like what is reported: that Abu Ayyub al-Ansari said to Umm Ayyub, "Do you not see what is being said?" She said:

"If you were in place of Safwan, would you have thought ill of the sanctity of the Messenger of God (ﷺ)?" He said, "No." She said:

"And if I were in place of ʿAʾisha, may God be pleased with her, I would not have betrayed the Messenger of God (ﷺ). ʿAʾisha is better than me, and Safwan is better than you."

[[His words end. He said: It is related that Abu Ayyub al-Ansari said to his wife, "Do you not see the talk of the people?" She said to him, "If you were in place of Safwan, would you have betrayed the sanctity of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) with evil?" He said, "No." She said, "And if I were in place of ʿAʾisha, I would not have betrayed him, and Safwan is better than you and ʿAʾisha is better than me." Ahmad said: And I have been inspired, by the light of faith, to this secret contained in the expression of other believers by "self," for she placed her husband in the position of Safwan and herself in the position of ʿAʾisha, then established for herself and her husband innocence and trustworthiness, until she established them for Safwan and ʿAʾisha by a stronger way, may God be pleased with her. It is possible, and God knows best, that the meaning differs from what al-Zamakhshari said: namely, that the expression with "selves" is literal, and the intention is to obligate the one who thinks ill to himself, because he did not rely on the restraint of faith regarding others, and neglected it and considered it regarding himself, and claimed innocence for her before knowing the ruling of desire rather than the ruling of guidance, and God knows best.]].

Which is to say: why was it not said, "Had you, when you heard it, thought well of yourselves and said..."? Why did he turn from address to the third person, and from the pronoun to the noun? I say: to intensify the rebuke by way of the shift (iltifat), and to state explicitly the word "faith," indicating that sharing in it requires that no believing man bear witness against his brother, nor any believing woman against her sister, by the saying of an absent person or a slanderer. And in it is an alert that the right of a believer, when he hears a saying about his brother, is that the matter be built upon assumption (zann), not upon doubt (shakk), and that he say outright, on the basis of his good assumption about the believer: ﴿This is a manifest lie﴾, in this very wording that declares the innocence of his standing, just as one who is certain and acquainted with the true state of affairs would say. This is part of the fine etiquette, of which few are the upholders and the guardians. Would that you found one who, when he hears, remains silent and does not spread what he heard among his sisters.

God made the distinction between a true accusation and a false one to rest on whether four witnesses are established or not. Those who accused Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her, did not have evidence for their claim, so the proof was established against them, and they were liars in the sight of Allah, that is, in His judgment and His law. This is a rebuke and reproach to those who heard the slander and did not find in themselves the will to repel it and deny it, and an argument against them based on what is plain and evident in the Sharia: the obligation to deem the slanderer a liar without evidence, and to punish him severely when he slanders a chaste woman among the women of the Muslims. How much more so, then, the mother of the believers, the truthful daughter of the truthful (Abu Bakr), the wife of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and the beloved of the Beloved of Allah.

Commentary of al-Zamakhshari (al-Kashshaf) on surah 24, verses 14–15:

*Lawla* (لولا) here is *al-ula* (الأولى), for exhortation (tahdid, urging), and *hadhihi* (هذه) is for the impossibility of one thing because of the existence of another. The meaning: "Had it not been that I decreed to bestow favour upon you in this world with various kinds of blessings, among which is granting you respite for repentance, and that I show mercy to you in the Hereafter with pardon and forgiveness, I would have hastened punishment upon you for what you plunged into of the tale of the lie (ifk)."

It is said: *afada fi'l-hadith* (أفاض في الحديث), *indafa'a* (واندفع), *wahada* (وهضب), and *khada* (وخاض). *Idh* (إذ) is an adverbial clause (zarf) governed by *massakum* (لمسكم), or by *afadtum* (لأفضتم). *Talaqqawnahu* (تَلَقَّوْنَهُ): one takes it from another. It is said: *talaqqa al-qawl*, *talaqqanahu*, and *talaqqafahu* (تلقى القول وتلقنه وتلقفه). From this is His saying, *fa-talaqqa Adamu min rabbihi kalimatin* (فَتَلَقَّى آدَمُ مِنْ رَبِّهِ كَلِماتٍ). It was also read according to the original form, *tatalaqqawnahu* (تتلقونه). *Wa-idh talaqqunahu*, with the assimilation of the dhal into the ta' (بإدغام الذال في التاء). [[The saying "wa-idh talaqqunahu" — perhaps its written form is thus "wa-itlaqqunahu," except if one considers what precedes the assimilation. (Ea.)]] *Talaqqunahu*, from *laqihu* in the sense of *laqafahu*. *Talaqqunahu*, from their casting it upon one another. *Talaqqunahu* and *tu'alliqunahu*, from *al-walq* and *al-alq*, which is lying. *Talaqqunahu* is related from Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her, and from Sufyan: "I heard my mother recite: *idh tathqafunahu*" [[The saying "I heard my mother recite *idha tathqafunahu*," and in another copy *tanqafunahu*, meaning "you follow it"; both copies are readings. (Ea.)]], and her father used to recite according to the letter of Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him.

If you ask: what is the meaning of His saying *bi-afwahikum* (بِأَفْواهِكُمْ), when speech is only with the mouth? I answer: its meaning is that a known matter has its knowledge in the heart, and the tongue expresses it. [[Mahmud said: "If you say speech is only with the mouths, what is the benefit of mentioning them? I answer: the intent is that this speech was not an expression of knowledge established in the heart, but merely a saying of the tongue." Ahmad said: It may be that the intent is hyperbole, or an allusion that one may speak boastfully while the one who speaks boastfully is not a certain, knowing person; and this is more severe and more decisive, and it is the secret that His saying indicates, *qad badati al-baghda'u min afwahihim* (قَدْ بَدَتِ الْبَغْضاءُ مِنْ أَفْواهِهِمْ). And Allah knows best.]] This lie is nothing but a saying that runs on your tongues and circulates in your mouths without being an expression of knowledge in the heart, like His saying, *yaqulna bi-afwahihim ma laysa fi qulubihim* (يَقُولُونَ بِأَفْواهِهِمْ ما لَيْسَ فِي قُلُوبِهِمْ), that is: you consider it a minor sin while it is with Allah a great sin that entails punishment. [[His saying "and it is with Allah a great sin that entails" — perhaps it is "entailing punishment." (Ea.)]] It is related from some of them that he became distressed at death, and when he was asked, he said: "I fear a sin that was not on my mind, and it is great with Allah." In the words of some of them: "Do not ever say of any of your evil deeds that it is small, for perhaps it is with Allah a palm tree, while it is with you a speck."

He described them as committing three sins and attached to them the touch of the great punishment. The first: the receiving of the lie by their tongues; that is, a man would meet another and say to him, "What is behind you?" and he would tell him the tale of the lie, until it spread and circulated, so that no house or assembly was left without it flying into it. The second: speaking about what they have no knowledge of. The third: their considering that trivial, and [it is] one of the great enormities.

Commentary of al-Zamakhshari (al-Kashshaf) on surah 24, verse 16:

If you say: How is it permissible to separate "lawla" (why not / if only) from "qultum" (you said)? I say: Adverbials of time and place have a special status, for they are treated as if they were the things themselves, since events occur within them and they are inseparable from them. Therefore, more latitude is allowed with them than with other words.

If you say: What is the benefit of placing the adverbial first so that it intervenes as a separator? I say: The benefit lies in showing that it was obligatory for them to refrain from speaking of the slander as soon as they heard it. Since mentioning the time was more important, it had to be placed first. If you say: What is the meaning of "yakun" (it is/would be), since the sentence would be complete without it, if it were said: "What is it for us to speak of this?"

I say: Its meaning is the meaning of "yanbaghi" (it befits), and "yasihhu" (it is proper), that is: "It does not befit us to speak of this, and it is not proper for us." A similar usage is: "It is not for me to say what is not true" (ma yakunu li an aqula ma laysa li bi-haqq). And "Subhanaka" (Glory be to You) is an exclamation of wonder at the greatness of the matter. [[Al-Zamakhshari said: "Its meaning is an expression of wonder at the greatness of the matter. Its origin is that when a person sees a marvel among the works of God Most High, he glorifies Him (sabbaha), and then it became frequent until it was used for everything that one marvels at. Here he introduced it as a question about their rebuke for abandoning wonder, saying:

If you say: Why was it permissible for the wife of a Prophet to be an unbeliever, like the wives of Noah and Lot, but not permissible for her to be immoral, and her unbelief was not something to marvel at while her immorality is something to marvel at? I say: Because the Prophets are sent to unbelievers in order to call them and win them over, and a wife's unbelief is neither an obstacle nor a repellent, unlike ... "kashkhana" (cuckoldry)." Ahmad said: What he raised as an objection is colder than this question, as if someone were to be puzzled about attributing indecency to someone like Aisha, which every sensible person denies and every discerning person marvels at. And God is the Granter of success.]]

If you say: What is the meaning of wonder in the word "tasbih" (glorification)? I say: The original basis of this is that one glorifies God upon seeing something marvelous among His works, and then it became frequent until it was used for everything one marvels at. Or it is to declare God free of having the household of His Prophet (peace be upon him) be immoral.

If you say: How was it permissible for the wife of a Prophet to be an unbeliever, like the wives of Noah and Lot, but not permissible for her to be immoral? I say: Because the Prophets are sent to unbelievers to call them and to win them over, so there must not be with them anything that repels people from them, and unbelief was not regarded by them as something repellent. As for "kashkhana" [[Al-Zamakhshari's word "kashkhana" seems to mean "dayyuthiyya" (cuckoldry). (ʿA)]], it is among the greatest repellents.

Yes, I can translate this passage. Here is the translation:

"That is, out of aversion to you returning, or lest you return, from your saying: 'I admonished so-and-so about such-and-such, and he left it.'

And [He] will punish them while they are still alive and legally responsible. And if you are believers, this is an incitement to them to take heed, and a reminder of what necessitates abandoning the return, namely their attribute of faith, which restrains from every ugly deed. And Allah makes clear to you the proofs of His knowledge and wisdom through what He sends down to you of the laws, teaches you of the beautiful manners, and admonishes you with the healing exhortations. And Allah is knowing of everything, doing what He does for the sake of wisdom."

And Allah is knowing of everything, doing what He does for the sake of wisdom."

The meaning: they spread the slander deliberately, intending its dissemination, desiring it and loving it. The punishment of this world is the prescribed penalty (ḥadd). The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) indeed lashed ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubayy, Ḥassān and Mistaḥ. Ṣafwān lay in wait for Ḥassān and struck him a blow with the sword, and it blinded his sight. It was also said: this is what is meant by His words ﴿And he among them who took upon himself the greater part thereof﴾. ﴿And Allah knows what is in the hearts of secrets and inner thoughts, and you do not know﴾, meaning: He has knowledge of the love of those who loved the spreading of the slander, and this is a punishment for it.

He repeated the favor by mentioning the withholding of immediate punishment, omitting the answer (jawab) of *lawla* (the apodosis of the conditional clause, "if not for...") just as he omitted it earlier. In this repetition, together with the omission of the answer, there is tremendous emphasis. The same is true of *al-Tawwab* (the Accepter of Repentance), *al-Ra'uf* (the Most Kind), and *al-Rahim* (the Most Merciful).

The fāḥisha and the faḥshā’ are that which is excessively ugly (al-fāḥisha wa-l-faḥshā’: mā afrata qubḥuhu). Abu Dhu’ayb said:

[[Wailing sounds rise from them with the nashīl (cooked meat),
as if they were co-wives of a Ḥarami woman, whose jealousy has grown excessive.

The pronoun refers to the cooking pots. Al-nashīj is the sound, like al-nay’ī. It is said: the pot wailed (nashajat al-qidr), and the weeper wailed (nashaja al-bākī). A nāshija stab wound is one that weeps blood. The bāʼ indicates accompaniment. Al-nashīl is cooked meat that is lifted out of the pot. That is: her jealousy has become excessive. Al-munkar is that which souls disapprove of, so they recoil from it and do not accept it. It has been read as khuṭuwāt, with the ṭāʼ vowelled with fatḥa and also with sukūn. Zakkā is read with tashdīd, and the pronoun refers to God, the Exalted. Had God not bestowed upon you His favour through the purifying repentance, not one of you would have been purified from the stain of the sin of the slander until the end of time. But God purifies the repentant by accepting their repentance when they make it pure, and He is All-Hearing of their words and All-Knowing of their inner thoughts and sincerity.

Translation:

This is from ائتلى (ta'allā), meaning to swear an oath: it is a form of افتعال (ifti'āl) derived from الألية (al-ālīya, "oath"). It has also been said that it derives from their saying: ما ألوت جهدا (mā alawtu jahdan, "I did not spare any effort"), when one does not withhold anything of it. The first meaning is supported by the reading of al-Hasan: ولا يتأل (wa-lā yata'all). The meaning is: let them not swear that they will not do good to those deserving of kindness. Or: let them not fall short in doing good to them, even if there is enmity between them because of a wrong they have committed. Let them return to them with pardon and forgiveness, and let them treat them as they hope their Lord will treat them, despite the abundance of their sins and offences. It was revealed concerning Mistah, who was the son of the maternal aunt of Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with them both. He was one of the poor among the Emigrants (muhajirun), and Abu Bakr used to spend on him. When he committed what he committed:

he swore that he would no longer spend on him. That was enough to call him to forbearance and to leave off requiting the one who does evil. It is related that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited it to Abu Bakr, and he said: "Yes, I love that Allah forgive me," and he returned his maintenance to Mistah and said: "By Allah, I will never withhold it from him again." Abu Haywa and Ibn Qutayb read: أن تؤتوا (an tu'tū), with the ta' (second person), as an iltifat (shift in grammatical person). Its support is His saying: ﴿Do you not love that Allah should forgive you?﴾ أَلا تُحِبُّونَ أَنْ يَغْفِرَ اللَّهُ لَكُمْ.

Al-Ghafilat (the unwary, the heedless) are those who are sound of breast and pure of heart, in whom there is no cunning or guile, because they have not tested affairs or experienced conditions, so they do not perceive what the experienced and knowing women perceive. He said:

"Indeed I have played with a tender girl, yielding and coquettish, a simple one (balha') who reveals to me her secrets."

[Lahawt: I amused myself and played. Bi-tifla (with a fatha on the ta'): meaning a soft, delicate woman; it is said "imra'a tifla al-anamil," i.e., her fingertips are soft and tender, meaning her tenderness and gentleness. Mayyala: haughty and coquettish. Balha': unwary, having neither guile nor cunning, and therefore she reveals to me her inner thoughts.]

And likewise the simple-minded (al-bulh) among men, in his (ﷺ) saying: "Most of the people of Paradise are the simple-minded (al-bulh)."

He married me while I was a virgin, and no one married a virgin other than me. He died while his head was in my lap, and he was buried in my house, and the angels surrounded him in my house. Revelation would descend upon him while he was with his wives, and they would scatter from him, and it would descend upon him while I was with him under his blanket. I am the daughter of his successor (khalifah) and his close friend (siddiq). My innocence descended from heaven. I was created good for a good man. And I was promised forgiveness and a generous provision."
